page: Microsoft Azure F48ams_v7 is a memory-intensive server instance belonging to the Famsv7 family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The instance features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs, utilizing a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, though it is premium storage capable, and it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the F48ams_v7 demonstrates top-tier performance, placing in the top 10% for both single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests, as well as Geekbench single-core and multi-core metrics. Its memory subsystem shows strong capabilities, with read-only small block memory bandwidth and large block write bandwidth scoring in the top 10%. This high-speed memory architecture supports intensive database operations and Redis SET operations, both of which rank in the top 10% of benchmarked systems. For specialized workloads, the processor's support for AVX-512 and vector neural network instructions enables strong performance in software compilation and image processing.

While the instance delivers top-tier performance in CPU-bound and memory-intensive tasks, its lack of local storage requires external premium storage attachments, which may impact overall I/O latency depending on the configuration. Additionally, while LLM inference speeds for small and medium models are strong to top-tier, performance drops to average levels for large 70B models due to the absence of dedicated GPU hardware. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated core allocation make it a resource-dense option for memory-intensive workloads without the overhead of GPU accelerators. It is highly suited for large-scale database operations, memory-cached key-value stores like Redis, software compilation pipelines, and medium-scale machine learning inference.
